data.title: A Bronze Age burial mound at Palárikovo in 3D
data.excerpt: After the Slavic sanctuary at Most pri Bratislave, our collaborator Igor Furugláš presents another unique 3D visualisation: the burial mound at Palárikovo. Pavel Dvořák explains why the rich Late Bronze Age warrior’s grave at the bottom of the mound held no body at all.

timeline.title: A warrior's cenotaph in the burial mound
timeline.description: The archaeologist Jozef Paulík examined the burial mound at Palárikovo and found a rich warrior’s grave at the bottom of it, in which, however, the dead man was not lying — it was a symbolic grave (a cenotaph) for someone who had died far away on a military campaign.

children.text: After the Slavic sanctuary at Most pri Bratislave we present you with another unique 3D visualisation from the workshop of our collaborator Igor Furugláš. The burial mound at Palárikovo.

When the archaeologist Jozef Paulík examined the burial mound at Palárikovo in southern Slovakia, which was to be levelled to the ground as part of land-drainage works, he discovered an unbelievably strange thing. At the bottom of the mound there was the rich grave of a warrior from the time of the Late Bronze Age, for whom the mound had indeed been built, but who was not lying in the grave. It is a so-called cenotaph, a symbolic grave which was built for a person who had died, for example, somewhere far away on a military campaign. It was believed that the dead without a grave do harm, and that is why a cenotaph was made for them and they were invited to enter.
